title: [finding] `Claim pointer:` is matched by NEITHER claim marker, and `latestClaimComment`'s header cites one as a claim the marker reads
body:
Filed unassigned by the os-dev seat working #12629 (`session_01MnijPVVDakqK2J335JoJtq`, branch `claude/issue-12629-family-member-patrol-row`). Out of that card's scope — different defect class, and the file's own ruling forbids the obvious repair — so it is recorded rather than fixed. Grading is the lane's.

## The measurement

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` has two claim markers and this live comment shape matches neither. Run against the shipped constants, with a positive control:

```
CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER  : false
CLAIM_NEAR_MISS_MARKER: false
nearMissClaimSeparators: []
governingClaim         : null
latestClaimComment     : null
control (canonical `Claim: PM loop round R6`): true
```

The subject string is `Claim pointer: folded into the 11678 family dispatch` — quoted in that file as a REAL line from its own claim census.

Why each misses: `CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER` is anchored `Claim(?:ed)?` then optional whitespace then a colon, and the word here is followed by ` pointer`. `CLAIM_NEAR_MISS_MARKER` requires the character after the word to be one of the four declared non-canonical separators (em dash, en dash, hyphen-minus, fullwidth colon); a lowercase letter is none of them. So the comment is invisible to H2, H20, H27, H33 and H34 alike.

## The part that is a straight factual error, not a coverage judgement

`latestClaimComment`'s docblock argues that it must NOT narrow to branch-naming claims, and offers two census specimens as claims the marker reads but that name no branch:

> the measured claim census carries 「Claim: PM loop round R6」 and 「Claim pointer: folded into the 11678 family dispatch」 — well-formed claims naming no branch of their own

The second one is not in that population at all. The paragraph's conclusion survives on the first specimen, so the code is right; the example is wrong, and it is the kind of wrong that propagates — a later author reading it will believe `Claim pointer:` is a shape the marker handles.

## Why this is not simply "widen the marker"

The maintainer's 2026-08-11 ruling makes the literal `Claim:` the single machine criterion, and `CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER`'s own note states the repair direction: the fleet converges on the documented spelling, and the predicate is ⛔ never relaxed. So `Claim pointer:` is a MALFORMED claim, not a dialect.

What follows from that is the actual gap: H34 exists precisely to make a malformed claim visible and point the seat at the canonical spelling — "visibility without redefining the vocabulary", in its own words — and it does not see this one either. A seat writing `Claim pointer:` gets no signal from anywhere, exactly as it did before H34 landed for the dash spellings.

## Disposition (candidate, for the lane to grade)

Two pieces, separable:

1. **Correct the docblock example.** Mechanical, and it removes a statement the code contradicts.
2. **Decide whether H34's near-miss shape should cover a WORD in the separator position**, not only a punctuation character. It is a real widening of the near-miss detector (never of the claim marker), and it needs its own noise measurement: `Claim` followed by a word is a much commoner prose opening than `Claim` followed by a dash, so the `looksLikeClaimContent` conservative half would be carrying more weight than it was measured for. ⛔ Not something to bolt on without that measurement — H34's header is explicit that its strictness was paid for once already.

Population size is unmeasured here; this seat found the shape quoted in the source, not by sweeping the board. A census of live `Claim <word>:` openings is the first thing a fix would need.
